counterfactual_missing_items: No biopsy or histopathologic confirmation of carcinoma is reported.
No systemic sinonasal, pulmonary, renal, or vasculitic findings support GPA.
No diabetic/immunocompromised/severely painful external otitis context supports necrotizing otitis externa.
decisive_items: 4-year history of right aural fullness that began after an acute upper respiratory tract infection
polypoid mass occluded the right external auditory canal with purulent discharge
irregularly enhancing mass in the right ear canal, middle ear cavity, and mastoid air cells, with erosive changes of the skull base and extension into the right middle cranial fossa
response.rationale: R6 better integrates the full sequence: chronic inflammatory middle-ear disease after URI and PE tube, painless otorrhea with an aural polyp, and temporal-bone destruction with intracranial extension. R5 and C1 rely almost solely on the aggressive imaging mass but omit the antecedent chronic inflammatory/canal polyp pattern that strongly favors cholesteatoma; R4 is a less specific re-labeling; R1 and R2 do not fit the unpromoted infection/age/systemic phenotype.

rejected.why: GPA requires systemic vasculitic involvement and is not supported by the URI-triggered chronic effusion, PE-tube treatment, aural polyp, and isolated temporal-bone destructive mass.

Aggressive chronic otitis media is a broad descriptive category that includes cholesteatoma; R6 is the more complete and specific mechanical diagnosis explaining the polyp, erosion, and intracranial extension.

Necrotizing otitis externa usually affects older or diabetic and immunosuppressed subjects with a primarily external-canal infectious picture; this case localizes beyond the canal and EB us into the middle ear/mastoid.
It is only an append-only completion of R5 with the same imaging span and no independent histologic or clinical raw evidence that would distinguish carcinoma from complicated cholesteatoma.
